description:
Research platform for stochastic reactor-physics algorithms on random media (dispersion fuel, TRISO, burnable-poison particles), per the 'OUTRAM-MC Design Scaffold v0.1' (Theodore Ong, Zhe Chuan Tan). Target methods: CLS, LCLS, EMCLS, SCLS, Adaptive-SCLS, homogenization, variance reduction.

SCOPE RECONCILIATION (design doc vs existing code): the doc proposes a standalone 9-crate 'outram-mc' workspace re-implementing geometry, materials, particle tracking and k-eigenvalue from scratch. Those already exist and are OpenMC-ported in crates/outram-mc-libs (geometry/, material/, particle/, physics/keff.rs, rng/, tally/). Doc sections 6-10 and 12 are therefore ALREADY DONE and are not re-scaffolded: Phase I surfaces/cells (geometry/surface.rs, cell.rs), Material (material/), Neutron state (particle/), power-iteration k-eff (physics/keff.rs), and explicit RSA (pebble_beds/stochastic_media.rs::pack_spheres, closed as op-6tz.25).

The genuinely new research content is doc sections 11 and 13-17, which this epic covers, built ON the existing port inside pebble_beds/ rather than as a parallel workspace.
title: outram-mc — stochastic-media MC research platform (CLS / SCLS / Adaptive SCLS)

description: Wrap the verified 0-D point-kinetics core (op-p6p.2) with GeN-Foam's full pointKineticNeutronics: Doppler + fuel/clad/coolant/structure T/rho feedback fields on fvMesh, GEM + control-rod-driveline reactivity, external neutron source w/ power-monitoring modulation, FMU inputs, liquid-fuel precursor advection. Needs common/timeProfile + neutronics base + multiRegion.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Done. Added multi_region/reactivity_feedback.rs: ReactivityFeedback layer turning mesh TH/TM feedback fields (fuel temperature, structure temperature, coolant density) into a scalar Delta-rho via an importance-weighted (volume or phi^2-worth) volume average of per-cell contributions. FeedbackTerm enum (no dyn): Doppler (linear or logarithmic law), Expansion (T_struct), Density (coolant/void, per-fractional-density). Generalises the lumped alpha*(T-Tref) Doppler already in outer_iteration to spatial fields; reduces to it exactly for a uniform field + volume weight. weighted_mean() also collapses TFuel to the feedback point MeshNeutronics uses for XS re-materialization, tying op-p6p.10 to op-p6p.8.4. V&V (release): uniform field -> lumped -3.0e-3; spatial profile negative feedback -3.0e-3; multiterm superposition (Doppler+density cancel to 0) and log-law within 2.7% of linear. NOTE: GEM/control-rod driveline, external neutron source, FMU inputs, and liquid-fuel precursor advection from the full pointKineticNeutronics are NOT ported here (filed as op-p6p.10 follow-ups below).

title: genfoam: pointKinetics reactivity-feedback + coupling layer (mesh/TH/GEM/FMU/liquid-fuel)

description:
The kinetics layer uses an ILLUSTRATIVE alpha_f = -4.0e-5 /K (kinetics.rs, TemperatureCoefficient::new::<per_kelvin>(-4.0e-5)). The published HTR-10 value is derivable and is roughly TWICE as strong.

DERIVATION (IAEA-TECDOC-1382 part 2, problem B2, original benchmark, VSOP; full core, helium, no rods). The document gives k_eff at three core temperatures, so rho = (k-1)/k gives the isothermal temperature coefficient directly:

  T degC     k_eff       rho (dk/k)
    20.0   1.119747    0.1069411
   120.0   1.110435    0.0994520
   250.0   1.095961    0.0875588

  20 -> 120 degC :  -7.49 pcm/K
 120 -> 250 degC :  -9.15 pcm/K
  20 -> 250 degC :  -8.43 pcm/K   <- use this as the linear value

So -8.427e-5 /K, versus the -4.0e-5 /K in the model: the model's feedback is 2.11x TOO WEAK. At beta = 0.0065 that is -0.01296 $/K published against -0.00615 $/K modelled.

NOTE THE COEFFICIENT IS NOT LINEAR -- it strengthens with temperature (-7.49 -> -9.15 pcm/K). A single linear alpha understates the feedback exactly where it matters most, at high temperature. Worth considering a two-point or piecewise form rather than one constant.

CAVEAT ON WHAT THIS IS: B2 is an ISOTHERMAL coefficient (whole core at one temperature), not a fuel-only Doppler coefficient. It bundles fuel, moderator and reflector. For a point-kinetics model whose single lumped node represents the whole core, the isothermal value is arguably the MORE appropriate one -- but the doc comment must say which it is, because calling an isothermal coefficient 'Doppler' would be wrong.

SECOND FINDING, and it matters for expectations: even with the correct coefficient, nulling the +16.45 $ cold clean excess needs a 1269 K temperature rise (against 2673 K with the illustrative value). Both are past the 1230 degC fuel limit. So fixing alpha does NOT make the model survive an instantaneous full-bank withdrawal.

The real HTR-10 safety demonstration test (control-rod withdrawal WITHOUT scram, docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md line 144) therefore cannot be an instantaneous full-bank withdrawal -- it must be a rate-limited withdrawal of part of the bank. That is what the rod DRIVE SPEED represents, and the drive speed currently in the widget is itself illustrative and unsourced (op-qeih). Sourcing the actual test procedure and rod speed is what would let this simulator attempt that benchmark.

title: htgr_sim_v1: temperature coefficient is 2.1x too weak — derive it from TECDOC-1382 B2
